chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn al-Walid ibn Sabih, from his father who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Walid! Where is your shop in relation to the Masjid?' So I said, 'By its door'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever you intend to go to your shop, so begin with the Masjid, and pray two Rak'at therein, or four.'
Then say, 'I came with the Might of Allah and His Strength, and I came without any might from me nor strength, but, by Your Might and Your Strength, O Lord.'
O Allah, I am Your servant seeking from Your Grace just as You Commanded me, therefore Make that to be easy for me, and I am free from anxiety in Your well-being'.
ai.seo_question: What supplication and prayer should one recite before going to work or shop to seek livelihood?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a spiritual protocol for merchants, linking the physical act of seeking sustenance with the spiritual discipline of prayer. The instruction to begin with two or four Rak'at in the Masjid underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating daily commerce with divine remembrance, while the specific supplication highlights the theological balance between human effort and reliance on Allah's power (Hawl) and strength (Quwwah).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Ibn Al-Waleed Bin Sabeeh, from his father who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Waleed! Where is your shop from the Masjid?’ So I said, ‘By its door’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever you intend to go to your shop, so begin with the Masjid, and pray two Rak’at therein, or four,

then say, ‘I came with the Might of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Strength, and I came without any might from me nor strength, but, by You<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Strength, O Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds.

I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant seeking from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Grace just as You<sup>azwj</sup> Commanded me, therefore Make that to be easy for me, and I am free from anxiety in Your<sup>azwj</sup> well-being’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Afi ibn af-Hakam from ibn af-Wafid ibn Sabih from his father who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked me, ‘Where is your shop in relation to the Masjid?’ I replied, ‘It is near the door of the Masjid.’ He then said, ‘When you want to go to your shop, first go to the Masjid, perform two or four Rak‘at Salah (prayer)
and at the end say, “I have attended this morning by the means and power of Allah, but not by my own means and power, in fact it is by Your means and power O Lord.

O Allah, I am Your servant and I appeal to You to grant me (wealth) through Your generosity, as You have commanded me to pray to You and appeal. Make this possible for me with ease, so I can be affluent and in good health by Your help.’””
